changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 7 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7070-no-invented-gantt-date-fields.md`

- names `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` — the console object page. The inline branch becomes `ganttViewOptions`, the sibling of `calendarViewOptions` and `timelineViewOptions`: the declared block spread whole, title floored at `'name'`, no date field invented. - `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — the render branch AND the capability gate. - `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `generateViewSchema`, the authored `object-view` element route, which bypasses `ListView` entirely.

### `.changeset/7499-gantt-non-axis-floors-omitted.md`

- names `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — the `object-gantt` render branch. - `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `generateViewSchema`, the authored `object-view` element route, which bypasses `ListView` entirely.

### `.changeset/7773-kanban-adapter-groupfield-write.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Who is NOT affected — the boundary is node-local.** Every VIEW-LEVEL `groupField` read is untouched and still live: it is a legacy alias of the spec's `groupByField` on the kanban *view config*, mapped by `normalize-list-view.ts`, and both adapters still resolve lanes through it (`ObjectView.tsx`'s `kanbanCfg.groupField ||`, `ListView.tsx`'s `groupByField || groupField`). Authoring `options.kanban.groupField` on a `list-view` or `object-view` keeps working exactly as documented in `packages/plugin-list/README.md`. `groupField` is dead only on the generated `object-kanban` NODE.

### `.changeset/7780-object-kanban-record-source.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`groupBy` is untouched and stays REQUIRED** (objectui#7322, PR #7774). A record source and a lane key are different questions: every lane-less document above is still refused at `groupBy`, and the two readings PR #7774 excluded from counting as a lane-less mode — the `dataSource` json fragment in `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx` and `ListView.tsx`'s runtime-generated node — are asserted still-refused in the new pin. The retired `groupField` tombstone is likewise still refused by name.

### `.changeset/8990-object-kanban-groupby-optional.md`

- names `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` **generates** the node as `groupBy: laneField`. `objectDef` loads asynchronously, so `laneField` is `undefined` on every load until it lands, and stays `undefined` whenever the object offers no `stageField` hint and none of `status` / `stage` / `state` / `phase`. The renderer serves that node; both published faces refused it. - `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx` documents an `object-kanban` node that is exactly `{ type, dataSource }`, with no `groupBy`. ⚠️ This one is weaker and is cited for what it is: that fragment is **still** refused after this change, at `RECORD_SOURCE_REQUIRED`, because `dataSource` is not a rung of the record-source ladder. It shows a lane-less board is a documented authoring; it is not a document this change admits.

### `.changeset/list-user-actions-collision-5398.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > The harvest now reads the object block only. Both `userActions` read sites in `ListView.tsx` carry a comment naming the collision, and `__tests__/ListView.userActionsCollision.test.tsx` pins each clause of it: the two shapes, a producer that manufactures the view one, the harvest's blindness to it, and the projection that must keep the object's operand with a toolbar block — or an empty block — present on the view.

### `.changeset/listview-comment-pair-4559.md`

- names `ListView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Two comment corrections in `ListView.tsx` (objectui#4559, objectui#4966). No runtime behaviour changes and the emitted bundle is byte-identical; the published `.d.ts` does change, which is why this is a `patch` rather than an empty frontmatter.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `00715f5ba` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1417 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1997 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36100256717)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a966cf01edd6ff0154441e41382d5364720b2dd4`

Rendered by an isolated review subagent spawned by the `domain:ui#4` seat; its served tier was checked against its transcript stamps (97 of 97 model stamps at the review tier). Adopted by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) The withhold: one decision point, the objectui#10477 spelling.** At head, `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` declares `const searchlessViewOnScreen = currentView === 'tree' || currentView === 'chart'` directly under `datasetChartOnScreen` (the const PR objectui#10477 added), and exactly two readers consume it: `showSearch: ua?.search !== false && !searchlessViewOnScreen` inside the `toolbarFlags` memo, whose dependency list now names the primitive, and the derived `const searchTerm = searchlessViewOnScreen ? '' : searchInput`. Both toolbar render sites (the separator and the popover trigger) read `toolbarFlags.showSearch`; the only other `showSearch` in the file is the pre-existing `showSearch: false` child-node prop in `baseProps`. The chart half keys on the view kind alone, so both the object-bound and the dataset-bound binding are withheld, which objectui#10477 had not done (its `showSearch` stayed `ua?.search !== false`). The applied-term half follows from the ruling rather than exceeding it: with the control withheld, a restored or carried term would go on narrowing `ListView`'s own fetch (the record-count bar reads that fetch's rows, and the export sends `search: searchTerm`) with nothing on screen to show or clear it, the same defect inverted (A4). It is documented in the changeset and pinned. One observation for the seat, not a breach: objectui#10477 did not gate the applied Filter on a dataset chart (its own comment names the record-count bar as the effective filter's only reader), so main now carries an asymmetry where a restored Filter still narrows the count bar on a dataset chart while a restored Search does not. That is outside this card.
- **(b) The kept term: sound.** The typed or restored value lives in `searchInput`; `handleSearchChange` is the only writer of `setSearchInput` and the only caller of `onSearchChange`, and no effect calls either on a view change. Every reader in `ListView.tsx` reads the derived `searchTerm`: the `$search` on the fetch, the client-side filter for inline `schema.data`, the fetch dependency list, the `pageResetSignature`, `ganttSearchTerm`, the export's `search` and its dependency list, the trigger's active keyword, the popover input, and the empty-state `hasActiveQuery`. So on tree and chart nothing narrows, the empty-state copy does not claim a search, and on a switch back the same value applies again with the keyword visible on the trigger. `ListViewHandle` exposes only `refresh`; there is no URL sync or analytics reader in the file. The old name `setSearchTerm` survives nowhere in `plugin-list` at head (the three remaining hits are `plugin-grid`'s own unrelated state). App-shell's `ObjectView` writes storage only through `onSearchChange` (keyed per user, object and view id) and restores through `initialSearchTerm`, so a term stored before this change on a tree view is restored, held, and not applied; nothing is dropped from storage. One consequence, stated in the changeset: on tree or chart a held term cannot be cleared until the user returns to a view that offers Search.
- **(c) Other views unchanged (A5).** The source diff touches only the new const and its comment, the `showSearch` line and the memo deps, the state rename and derived term, `handleSearchChange`, and one comment line above `ganttSearchTerm`. For grid, kanban, calendar, gallery, timeline, map and gantt, `searchlessViewOnScreen` is false, so `searchTerm` equals `searchInput` and `showSearch` equals `ua?.search !== false`, byte-for-byte today's behaviour. Six of the seven are pinned present in the new file, grid is the CONTROL twice.
- **(d) The pins are real.** The new file holds 17 cases: 1 grid CONTROL for presence, 3 absence cases (tree, object-bound chart, dataset-bound chart), 6 presence cases (kanban, calendar, gallery, timeline, gantt, map), 2 `userActions.search: true` cases, 1 grid CONTROL for a restored term reaching the fetch and the trigger, 3 restored-term cases asserting `$search` undefined on every host fetch after at least one fetch, and 1 switch case. The reverse-proof legs are exactly what that list predicts: both halves removed reddens the 3 absence, 2 `true`, 3 restored-term and switch cases (9) and leaves the 2 CONTROLs and 6 presence cases green (8); visibility only reddens the 3 absence, 2 `true` and switch cases (6); applied term only reddens the 3 restored-term cases and the switch case (4). None is vacuous: every case first awaits its view's stand-in, the absence cases assert a testid the CONTROL proves exists, the restored-term cases demand a fetch before asserting on it, and the switch case asserts the term reaches the fetch on grid, leaves it on tree and on chart, returns on grid with the keyword on the trigger, and that `onSearchChange` was called exactly once with `needle`. The `true` pair repeats the absence assertion under an authored key; it pins the fold (A3), which is its stated purpose. I did not re-run the suite (rule); CI Test shards 1 to 8 are green on the head.
- **(e) Changeset truth.** `.changeset/10326-toolbar-search-withheld-tree-chart.md`: every sentence holds at head. The tree's own `find` in `packages/plugin-tree/src/ObjectTree.tsx` sends `$filter`, `$top` and `$expand` and no `$search`; `packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.tsx` calls `ds.aggregate` and `ds.queryDataset` with no search parameter; the control is not rendered on either view whatever the chart binding; an authored `userActions.search: true` folds to the default (`normalize-list-view.ts` maps legacy `showSearch` to `userActions.search`, and the flag reads `!== false`); the seven other views keep it; a set term is not applied to the fetch or the export on those views; the term is kept and `onSearchChange` is not called for the switch. No line-address citation. One precision note: the defect paragraph is scoped by its antecedent (views that draw what they query for themselves); the unauthored inline-data tree, where the term did narrow drawn rows, sits outside that scope and is covered by the bullets, which are unconditional. The corrected `.changeset/10250-self-querying-views-toolbar-state.md`: frontmatter sha256 `50217e32b34f68c29d9a73407eebbff61cc63d5cbc605ffb722af4c0dbc12876` on both the base blob and the head blob, byte-identical; the corrected last paragraph is true at head (toolbar state still reaches no dataset-chart query; the Search box still reaches no tree or chart query; objectui#10326 stops offering it there); the correction was forced, because the old sentence presupposed a Search box on tree and chart that head no longer offers and would have published that presupposition into the CHANGELOG. The seven pending changesets the claims gate flagged (7070, 7499, 7773, 7780, 8990, `list-user-actions-collision-5398`, `listview-comment-pair-4559`) were re-read: none says anything about the toolbar Search; none is falsified. My own grep finds an eighth naming `ListView.tsx`, `gantt-owns-data-comment-7222.md`, which the gate skips by design (empty frontmatter, never publishes); it is about `ganttOwnsData` and is not falsified either. `.changeset/10327-dataset-chart-view-filter.md` is still pending, Filter-only, still true. The wider mentions (8317's `userActions.search !== false` fallback quote, 7924's legacy `showSearch` mapping table, 8254, 8970) are all still true.
- **(f) Clause-② `no` holds.** `packages/plugin-list/package.json` and the package index are untouched; the `export` lines of `ListView.tsx` are identical between the merge-base and head; `ListViewProps` and `ListViewHandle` are not in the diff; no `@object-ui/types` file is touched. No exported symbol, type or accept set moves.
- **(g) The seat's answers.** Q1 A is right. Who loses what: a list view with an inline `data` block, no `objectName` and no data source, drawn as a tree. That shape is authorable (the TS face has `objectName?` optional under a record-source presence rule) but authored nowhere in this tree: at head, `viewType` set to `tree` occurs only in two test files, none in `examples`, `docs` or `apps`; the console's `ObjectView` sets `objectName: objectDef.name` on the schema and passes `dataSource={ds}`, so every console tree queries for itself. On that unauthored shape, `ListView` hands its client-side-filtered rows down as `data` and `ObjectTree` draws them, so the term used to narrow the rows while cutting the hierarchy, the very cost the triage named.
